newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light unit advances in China deal.
newsitem.headline: China Light unit advances in China deal.

text.p: China Light and Power Co Ltd said on Sunday its wholly-owned unit China Energy Investment Co Ltd and Exxon Energy Ltd had signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on participation in the development of a 1,050 megawatt gas-fired power plant project in Shenzhen.

The project in the southern Chinese boom town of Shenzhen was still under negotiation and the MOU was a basis for continuation of project feasibility studies and ongoing discussion with all parties concerned, China Light said in a statement.
Under the MOU signed on October 31, the two companies would have a 35 percent interest in the project.

The other investors were Shenzhen Qianwan Electric Power Development Co Ltd, Guangdong Electric Power Holding Co, and Kanematsu Power (South China) Co Ltd. The statement did not say if they took part in the MOU signing.
The power plant would consist of three units of 350 MW class combined-cycle gas turbine and was expected to become operational by the end of the century.
Castle Peak Power Co Ltd, owned by China Light and Exxon Energy, was engaged in preliminary discussions regarding the re-supply of gas to the Shenzhen project, the statement said.
China Light and Exxon Energy have been in a joint venture in the power generation business in Hong Kong for more than 30 years.
